hints: Take x along the current and y across it. Find x(t) and y(t) separately, then eliminate t.
worded:
1. Take x along the current and y across. The swimmer’s acceleration relative to the water is 2t across, starting from rest.

2. Across: v_y = t², so y = t³/3.

3. Along: the water carries the swimmer at v, and he has no velocity of his own along the current, so x = vt.

4. Eliminate t = x/v: y = (x/v)³/3 = x³/(3v³). (D)

5. Check: early on the swimmer has almost no velocity across, so the path must leave the bank tangent to the flow; y ∝ x³ does. Also x/v is a time, so only (D) gives y ∝ t³ as found.
conventional:
![](asset:P000283-sol-1)

$$\frac{dv_{y}}{dt} = 2t,\ v_{y}(0) = 0 \Rightarrow v_{y} = t^{2} \Rightarrow y = \frac{t^{3}}{3};\quad\quad x = vt.$$

$$y = \frac{1}{3}\left( \frac{x}{v} \right)^{3} = \frac{x^{3}}{3v^{3}}.$$
mistakes: Integrate twice from rest: v_y = t², y = t³/3 (not t²).
Replace t by x/v, so v appears cubed.
